brief: This week 11 new startups joined the list, which now has 50 companies on it. The strongest newcomer is Precision Neuroscience, which makes a thin brain implant that reads brain signals to help people with paralysis control computers, and it shows that a gentler version of a scary technology can reach patients sooner. The trend of the week is security for the AI era, with startups building tools that find, watch and control the new risks created by cloud, data and AI agents.
gaps: Nobody serves the physical trades or construction: Maven Robotics and Dexory automate warehouses, but a robot or AI tool for site inspection, plumbing or electrical work is an open niche.

No entry targets Africa, South Asia or Latin American health: Aqemia, Enveda and Evvy are all in rich markets, so a low-cost AI diagnostic or drug-discovery tool built for tropical diseases or local clinics is missing.

Nothing combines AI note-taking with other regulated professions: Nabla, Tandem Health and Lawhive cover doctors and lawyers, but social workers, teachers and insurance adjusters drown in the same paperwork.

Agriculture and climate lack AI-science players: CuspAI and Cradle design materials and proteins, but nobody uses that method for crop traits, soil microbes or fertiliser alternatives alongside xFarm's farm data.

Security for physical and critical infrastructure is thin: Exein and Reco secure devices and AI agents, but no one pairs this with ports, water utilities or power grids, which Mazama Energy and Crusoe will make more AI-dependent.

trends.name: Security for the AI era
trends.sentence: Startups build cybersecurity tools that find, watch and control risks created by cloud, data and AI agents.

trends.name: Hardware for the AI boom
trends.sentence: Startups remove physical bottlenecks in AI computing, from chips and light-based links to networking and data centers.

trends.name: AI agents doing whole jobs
trends.sentence: Startups package AI as agents or easy tools that carry out complete tasks like coding, calls, hiring and automation.

trends.name: AI for science discovery
trends.sentence: Startups point AI at slow lab searches to find new drugs, proteins, materials and faster engineering designs.

trends.name: Space and defense hardware
trends.sentence: Startups build satellites, capsules, drones and planning software for government and defense customers.

trends.name: AI note-taking for clinicians
trends.sentence: Startups use AI to cut doctors' paperwork by writing notes and reports from visits and scans.
